rationale: The frozen candidate carried the two role-isolated advisory inputs standard-lesson-v3 requires, from distinct agent runs and distinct model families, both pinned to the same candidate commit. The academic review returned request-changes with five major and two minor findings; the learning-design review approved with three notes and no requested change. Every academic finding was a bounded correction to a stated claim, an objective, or an answer key rather than a rebuild of the lesson's structure, so the maintainer repaired them in place rather than returning the pack for re-authoring. One finding could not be resolved as the reviewer proposed: the point estimates it attributed to a published correction could not be confirmed, because the correction's text is not reachable through this project's permitted routes and the article of record displays different figures again. Rather than assert either set, the lesson now carries the direction and the fact of both differences and records the correction's existence. The academic verdict is preserved as dissent, and neither reviewer is represented as having approved these repairs.
dissent: The academic review's request-changes verdict stands as material dissent from the 0.1.0 candidate as reviewed. Its findings were incorporated by the maintainer after review; no reviewer has seen or approved the repaired text.
conditions: The maintainer commits the repaired content first and stamps that exact commit as finalCommit, making no teaching-content change afterward.
Strict source preflight and full validation must pass on the final content before merge.
The publication transition for status, sourceConfidence and claim reviewStatus is the maintainer's separate act and is not authorised by this decision.

materialChanges: Restricted the clock test to sentences reporting an observation, and stated that reported material stays in the record carrying its own source and period; rewrote the dependent objective.
Replaced the claim that mood and affect are not evidence for each other with separate attribution, and named holding them side by side as what congruence means.
Corrected the account of 'denies' to a conventional record of a reported absence whose cost is compression, and applied the same correction to the table row and the 'refused water' line.
Narrowed the affect claim and objective to the range, intensity and congruence the cited chapter supports, and presented reactivity as an observation to record alongside the term labile.
Removed the congruence judgement from the keyed answer of item-mood-and-affect-line and scored bounded separate attribution instead.
Removed both stigmatising-language point estimates as unverifiable, retained the direction of both differences, and recorded the correction notice in the reference locator.
Bounded the prevalence sentence to at least one term from the study's restricted descriptor lists.

evidenceChecked: All seven scenes keep one level-one heading, semantic Markdown, linear reading order and text-first instruction, with no raw HTML, embeds or executable content.
The pack carries no images or diagrams, so no alternative text obligation arises; the repaired tables remain readable in linear order.
All six sources are used facts-only with no reuse of source expression; the StatPearls chapter's CC BY-NC-ND terms are respected by that limitation.
The repaired stigmatising-language passage removes figures that could not be verified rather than restating them, which lowers rather than raises the pack's rights and accuracy exposure.
limitations: The audit is a maintainer reading of the repaired text, not an independent accessibility or rights review; the accessibility-rights role was not staffed for this tier.
No screen-reader or assistive-technology run was performed against the rendered lesson.

One reviewer finding could not be closed on the evidence the reviewer proposed: the correction carrying the disputed point estimates is not reachable through permitted routes, so the pack asserts no figure from that study rather than adopting either set.
